question: Why would losing sharks throw the whole sea off balance?
answer: Sharks sit at the top of the food chain and keep the fish below them in check. Take them away and their prey multiply, so every level beneath tips out of balance. Yet about 100 million sharks and rays die every year.
move: A top predator is the brake: remove it and the whole food web runs out of balance.
